{{Short description|American mathematician and historian (1926–2026)}}
[[File:Curtis charles w.jpg|thumb|Charles W. Curtis]]
'''Charles Whittlesey Curtis''' (October 13, 1926 – May 3, 2026) was an American mathematician and [[history of mathematics|historian of mathematics]], known for his work in [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]] and [[representation theory]]. He was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Oregon]].

==Life and career==
Curtis received a bachelor's degree from [[Bowdoin College]] in 1948,<ref>[http://uocatalog.uoregon.edu/liberalarts/Mathematics University of Oregon Catalog 2011–2012] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720102613/http://uocatalog.uoregon.edu/liberalarts/Mathematics |date=July 20, 2011 }}, retrieved 2011-07-11.</ref> and his Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1951, under the supervision of [[Nathan Jacobson]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4301}}</ref> He taught at the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison]] from 1954 to 1963.<ref>[http://www.math.wisc.edu/oldhome/people/AllFac.html UW Math Department Faculty 1849-2010] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829194822/http://www.math.wisc.edu/oldhome/people/AllFac.html |date=2012-08-29 }}, retrieved 2011-07-11.</ref> Subsequently, he moved to the [[University of Oregon]], where he was an [[emeritus professor]].<ref>[http://math.uoregon.edu/people/emeritus.php Emeritus Faculty Directory] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427182304/http://math.uoregon.edu/people/emeritus.php |date=2012-04-27 }}, University of Oregon Department of Mathematics, retrieved 2011-07-11.</ref>

While at Yale, on June 17, 1950 in [[Cheshire, Connecticut]], Curtis married his wife Elizabeth, a [[kindergarten]] teacher and childcare provider. At the time of their 50th anniversary in 2000, they had three grandchildren.<ref>{{citation|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=O1dWAAAAIBAJ&pg=3766,6703564|title=Curtis|journal=Eugene Register-Guardian|date=July 24, 2000}}.</ref>

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>

Curtis died in [[Eugene, Oregon]], on May 3, 2026, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite news |title=Charles Curtis |url=https://www.registerguard.com/obituaries/pore1483880 |access-date=21 May 2026 |publisher=The Register-Guard |date=20 May 2026}}</ref>

==Research==
Curtis introduced [[Curtis duality]], a [[duality (mathematics)|duality]] operation on the [[character (mathematics)|character]]s of a [[reductive group]] over a [[finite field]]. His book with [[Irving Reiner]] {{harv|Curtis|Reiner|1962}} was the standard text on representation theory for many years.
